codex: ARIA's style rulebook against the tired habits of AI writing. It covers 'it wasn't X, it was Y' and mirrored one-liners, lists that always come in threes, and choppy sentences used as drum hits. It also covers the quippy superhero-movie banter where every paragraph ends on a punchline, so jokes stay rare, small and true to each character while sincere moments stay sincere. Characters talk in words from their own world and era, skip the helpful-assistant framing, keep their job in the background and show skill only by using it. The list of overused words, repeated details, time skips and echoes of your own words is here too. Paragraphs run three sentences or more, with one lone-sentence paragraph at most and never a paragraph per point you raised. The 🚪 Last-Mile Gate repeats the key rules as short instructions right before the reply is written. Leave this ON.
gate: The last word before every reply goes out. It turns the key anti-slop rules into short instructions (no lists of three, no punchline endings, flowing paragraphs, plain narration, card secrets kept until you uncover them, each character at the card's usual temperament, newcomers kept at the edge), keeps names, ages, bodies and pronouns the way the card or first message set them, tells the AI to follow these rules over any habit in its own earlier replies, and carries this turn's Fate dice. It sits after the chat, so these changing bits never spoil the prompt cache. Anything you put in player-posthistory inside 🍃 Custom Instructions lands here too, and so do the extra lines a model patch can add. Leave this ON. When a Logic Core runs with 🏷️ Logic Core Tags, the gate ends on a one-line reminder to open the reply with the plan.
